_comment: Per-state income-tax constants. SOURCE OF TRUTH for both the TypeScript engine (stateTaxRules.ts) and scripts/verify_plan.py — JSON so there is one file and two readers, no hand-duplication. Every constant must be verifiable against the primary source in `sources`. Review annually: see docs/5-state-tax-model.md.

GA.note: HB 463's further rate cuts (-0.125%/yr toward a 3.99% floor) and standard-deduction increases (+$375/+$750/yr) are CONTINGENT on revenue triggers, so both are frozen at their TY2026 values — see docs/5-state-tax-model.md §2 Rule 1. The TY2027 exclusion step-up to $70,000 is unconditional in the same bill, so it IS modeled. No age-65 addition to the standard deduction exists under the flat-tax structure. Constants come from the enacted bill text and IT-511, NOT the DoR web pages, which are stale and contradict each other on the earned-income sublimit.
GA.caveat: Georgia tax is likely overstated: HB 463's scheduled rate cuts and standard-deduction increases depend on state revenue triggers, so both stay frozen at TY2026 values (4.99%; $15,000 single / $30,000 married). Note that tax-smart withdrawals sized to the federal deduction floor can still owe Georgia tax before age 62, when the retirement exclusion has not yet begun. For couples, the per-person exclusion is applied to pooled household income, which over-excludes when only one spouse has retirement income.

NH.note: The Interest & Dividends Tax was repealed effective 1 Jan 2025 (HB 2, 2023 session), so NH taxes no individual income for TY2026 onward.

TN.note: The Hall income tax on interest and dividends was fully repealed for tax years beginning 1 Jan 2021.

WA.caveat: Washington has no income tax, but levies a 7% excise tax on long-term capital gains above an inflation-indexed standard deduction ($278,000 for 2025), with an additional higher tier. It is NOT modeled here: retirement accounts are exempt, so it reaches only taxable-brokerage gains, and this tool applies a flat cost-basis percentage per withdrawal rather than tracking realized gains.
